correctness.limitations: Existential deterministic scheduler with potentially unbounded gaps; the theorem gives no probability of failure under random activation and does not refute bounded-fairness results.
correctness.rationale: Starting at the unit singleton j, full copies first to j+1 and then to j leave the singleton at j+1; j−1 is distinct from both j and j+1 for n≥3. Each block starts with untouched zero and one anchors. Repeating the actual arc into i leaves the source unchanged and differs from full copy at its endpoint by (1−p_i)^N times the starting difference. Each finite N_m can make that error at most 2^(−m−4), and full copy is 1-Lipschitz in the sup norm, so the block-entry error is strictly below 1/8. The actual anchors never change within their block, proving the diameter bound also at every individual activation. Each arc appears twice per ideal rotation and each real block is finite and nonempty. On two vertices the gap is at most max_i(1−p_i)^t times its initial value, where the intended bound is [max_i(1−p_i)]^t; nested extrema then imply convergence. One vertex cannot fail, and strong connectivity for n≥3 needs at least n arcs, so the three-vertex three-arc example is minimal in both respects.
